To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the epitope-specificity of the antibodies in the sera is different for the healthy subjects, patients CHD, and patients IBD.
anti-HSP60/65 antibodies in CHD are specific to the human HSP60 protein, whereas anti-HSP60 in IBD are specific to the mycobacterial HSP65 protein.
the epitope specificities of the antibodies to human HSP60 are disease-specific.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the epitope specificity and the cross-reactivity of anti-HSP antibodies in the sera from healthy subjects, patients suffering from coronary heart disease and patients suffering from inflammatory bowel disease.
the epitope specificity and possible role of antibodies to HSP60 and HSC65 in various diseases.

the development of a diagnostic tool to detect the epitope specificities of anti-HSP antibodies in the sera and the identification of epitope specific antibodies in sera of healthy subjects and patients with various diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the presence of antibodies against the epitopes of the equatorial domain is specific for CHD and that the presence of the antibodies against epitopes in the C-terminal region of human HSP65 is specific for IBD.
the epitope specificities of anti-HSP antibodies are disease dependent.
the epitope-specificity of anti-HSP antibodies in the sera from patients with CHD and IBD is different from the epitope-specificities of anti-HSPs in healthy subjects.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the epitope recognition of anti-HSP antibodies is disease-specific.
the presence of antibodies directed against the same linear epitopes of HSP60/65 molecules in the sera of HP, CHD, and IBD patients indicates a common pathogenetic mechanism for all these diseases.
the epitopes of the anti-HPS60 antibodies are different in the sera of CHD patients compared to those of HP and that the epitopes are even more different in IBD patients.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the epitopes in the HSPs are differentially recognized in different diseases and the differences in the epitope specificity are likely to reflect the differences in the mechanisms of the formation and function of the anti-HSps antibodies.
the epitope-specificity of antibodies to human HSP60 is different from that to the mycobacterial HSP65.
the epitope specificities of the anti-Hsp60 and anti-Hsp65 antibodies in CHD and IBD patients are different from those in the sera of HPs.
